newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Yen gains sees vols push higher in Europe.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Yen gains sees vols push higher in Europe.

text.p: Yen option volatilities were higher in morning Europe as spot yen extended its recent gains, setting fresh highs against the mark and dollar.
Dealers said trade was volatile but confined to mainly the short end of the dollar/yen curve as players scrambled to hedge dollar downside exposure.
"Options trade is very choppy and directionless with most people trading defensively at the moment," said a U.S. bank options dealer.

Dollar/yen spot tested its lowest in nearly seven months in late Asia/early Europe, pressured by ongoing concerns over Japan's trade surplus and the implications it will have at next week's G7 summit in Denver.

These concerns were amplified by the announcement overnight of a 92.7 percent year-on-year rise in Japan's April current acccount surplus to 1.09 trillion yen. Although this figure was in line with market expectations, comments from U.S. Deputy Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers that Japan should avoid running up external surpluses fuelled dollar/yen bears.

One-month dollar/yen implied volatility was trading at 15.1/15.5 percent against 13.6/14.1 percent late Tuesday in Europe. One-week volatility was hiked back up to Monday's level of 18.0/20.0 percent.
The dollar/yen risk reversal, the difference in implied volatility of calls relative to puts, extended its bias for yen calls to 2.0/2.4 percent from 1.7/2.1 Tuesday.
The dollar's proximity to the key 110 yen level was likely to keep vols bid and a break below this point could see volatility climb even higher.

"We see too much emphasis being put on the U.S.-Japan trade issue and dollar/yen vols look overdone on that basis," said one trader. "A break of 110 probably will see vols knee-jerk higher but the extreme bias of the risk reversal won't last and should limit big vol gains from here."
Mark/yen spot slid to a fresh 22-month low, pushing one-month vol to 13.0/14.0 percent against 11.8/12.2 Tuesday. The risk reversal favours mark puts around 1.7/2.2 as against 1.2/1.6 on Tuesday.
Dollar/mark volatility was also higher but trade was subdued, with spot keeping to relatively narrow ranges.
One-month dollar/mark vols stood at 9.7/9.9 percent versus 9.3/9.6 on Tuesday. The risk reversal shifted its skew slightly to mark calls after trading around par earlier this week.

Mark cross vols were steady as activity was overshadowed by the yen's moves. However, doubts over Europe's monetary union timetable continue to circulate and dealers see volatilities well supported at current levels.

Mark/French franc vol stood at 2.2/2.5 percent across the curve out to one-year from 2.1/2.6 Tuesday. Mark/lira one-month was at 5.20/5.75 percent, rising to 5.35/5.70 one year out. Mark calls continue to be favoured in the risk reversals.
